verdict.rationale: MotherDuck lets users ask natural-language questions through its remote MCP server and Dives, without writing SQL (docs-26, docs-60, docs-4, docs-58). It grounds agent SQL with 'Guides', markdown documents holding org metric definitions and join conventions (docs-30). Governance comes from read-only MCP restriction and role- and include-pattern-scoped Shares (docs-31, docs-10, docs-11). However, Guides are advisory prompt context rather than an enforced semantic layer, so nothing guarantees joins cannot be hallucinated. Missing for 10: an enforced/governed semantic or metrics layer that constrains generated queries, evidence of answer accuracy or validation, and independent or hands-on corroboration that business users get grounded answers.
